maria: FYI we've started seeing traces that never link back to the gateway for async jobs processed after a retry. Noticed in production dashboards — entire child span trees orphaned. :thinking_face:
kevin: Seen that too. Guessing the visibility-timeout/retry path is dropping the W3C headers or truncating them in the message attributes. Which queue did you hit?
tanya: SQS FIFO and our internal job-queue both show the same pattern. The common denominator is the worker that re-enqueues the job on partial failure.
maria: Right — re-enqueue flow currently does `publish({ payload, metadata })` where metadata is a shallow copy; we were hitting attribute size limits so we stringify and gzip some fields. Might be our header encoding step.
kevin: Can we standardize on a compact propagation envelope instead of copying all of `traceparent` + `tracestate` + baggage into attributes? Suggestion: keep `traceparent` as raw header and put a single `x-rw-prop` attribute with base64(zlib(proto)) for extras. That stays within attribute size and is easy to decode.
dan: We also need a robust fallback so when header decode fails we don't lose causal link. Proposal: if worker can't parse incoming prop, attach a new span with tag `relinked_from:<incoming-id>` and emit a metric for those events. That lets us stitch in post-process if exporter has the original.
kevin: Example header mapping I sketched:%0A```
// gateway -> message attrs
"traceparent": "00-abcdef1234abcd-0123456789abcd-01",
"x-rw-prop": "<base64-zlib(proto)>",
// worker on receive: prefer traceparent, then decode x-rw-prop for baggage/tracestate
```
%0AIf decode fails, worker logs `trace.decode_failed` with the raw attr for later investigation.
tanya: How do we handle batching? A single batch can contain multiple requests with different trace ids. We can't shove all into one attr. For our batch protocol we should make per-item attrs inside the batch payload, not global attrs. Otherwise we get cross-contamination.
maria: Agree. For streaming/response batching we should preserve per-request traceparent at the item level. For our existing proto we can add an optional `trace_context` field per item.
kevin: Rollout plan: 1) implement decode/encode libraries in runtime (golang + node) behind feature flag; 2) have workers emit `trace.relink_attempt` metric and log sample of failed decodes; 3) enable on a small percentage of hosts, watch orphan-span rate in Tempo/Honeycomb; 4) ramp.
dan: Operational checks: add an alert if orphaned-root-span-rate > 0.5% over 5m or if `trace.decode_failed` spikes. Also add a daily job to correlate re-enqueue logs with orphan spans for automated stitching in tracing UI.
tanya: One more: sampling decisions. If gateway sampled=false, but worker later samples=true, we need to respect gateway's sampling or at least tag the child span with `gateway_sample_override` so we can filter. Otherwise counts will be inconsistent.
maria: Good call. We'll propagate `otlp.sampled` flag inside the compact envelope and prefer it. If worker is forced to sample for debugging we set `gateway_sample_override=true` and keep it as metadata.
kevin: Quick PR sketch (golang) for encode/decode function:%0A```
func encodeProp(tp, ts string, baggage map[string]string) string {
  p := PropProto{TraceParent: tp, TraceState: ts, Baggage: baggage}
  raw, _ := proto.Marshal(&p)
  cmp := compress(raw)
  return base64.StdEncoding.EncodeToString(cmp)
}

func decodeProp(b64 string) (PropProto, error) { ... }
```
%0Awe'll keep the proto tiny (ids + sampled + small baggage map) to avoid long attrs.
ops-bot: deploybot: will tag the feature flag rollout as `env=staging` -> `canary` -> `prod` and create a dashboard showing orphaned-span-rate and `trace.decode_failed` logs.
maria: Next steps: Kevin/Tanya to implement libs and a small worker patch, Dan to add alerts and dashboard widgets, I'll draft a runbook for stitch/fallback. Push an RFC to `eng-platform/rfcs` with the encoding proto and test vectors.
kevin: I'll open an RFC PR by EOD with binary examples and the encoding proto.
dan: I'll add the dashboard and alert in Grafana and link to the RFC.
maria: Thanks — let's keep the initial rollout conservative. If anyone sees high noise ping here. :thumbsup:
